translations.text: Alas, O God! Alas today, and alas yesterday! Alas tomorrow! Trembling has weakened me for fear of departing from this world.
Alas, O God, my two hands! Though for a while they were forever taking, though they are [?] now, they have done me great harm.
Alas for the dark, blind night! Alas for the bright day of trial! Alas, O God of heaven, for the danger that lies before me!
Alas, O God, my two sides and my two thighs together, my two calves that have changed colour, O King with the grace of the Holy Spirit!
Alas, O God, my two feet! Though they were once bold, they do not let me go out, so that I cannot walk.
Alas, alas! I am lighter than a log on a stream. I do not go around the stone church or the stone; I say nothing but 'ah' and 'alas'. Alas.
